newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks recoup losses, end barely changed.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks recoup losses, end barely changed.

text.p: SPI Futures 2760 -6.0 US 30yr cl 6.79 +0.05
10yrbond futs 92.965 +0.045 Gold NY 333.95 Lon fix 334.55
*Stocks recouped most of early losses to end barely changed from Monday's record levels. Volume 342.73 million, value A$854.42 million, 1,112 stocks traded, 296 steady, 426 up, 390 down.
Australian shares ended Tuesday barely changed from Monday's record levels, as the strong underlying sentiment won over an early bout of profit-taking on the first day of the new financial year.

"We had a very weak morning, and it was a good recovery to claw back all those early losses. It's a tricky time of year with a lot of book-squaring and people trying to take home profits," one Brisbane-based dealer said.
The All Ordinaries index closed 4.7 points lower at 2721.2, down from a record close of 2735.9 on Monday. Turnover reached a healthy A$854.4 million.
The September share price index futures contract was six points lower at 2,760, 38.8 points above the underlying index.

The Honk Kong handover had no impact on the Australian share market, dealers said, with most eyes on the upcoming two-day U.S. Federal Open Market Committe meeting and the outcome of Reserve Bank of Australia's monthly meeting earlier on Tuesday.
"I think some still hope for a (domestic) rate cut, but the chances have diminished," one dealer said.
The banking sector initially slumped in disappointment as no cut was announced this morning, but later recovered some losses to end 0.37 percent lower on the day.
Commonwealth Bank fell 16 cents to A$15.84, and Westpac Banking six cents to A$7.91, while National Australia Bank recovered completely to end 4.9 cents higher at A$19.019.
Profit-taking pulled down Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd in the early hours, but optimism over the giant's future earnings reversed losses. The stock ended 3.7 cents up at A$19.52.
Other blue chips were mixed, with miners Rio Tinto, down 11 cents to A$22.47 and WMC one cent up at A$8.36.
Among the winners were News Corp shares, which rose 12 cents to A$6.47 after its ADRs firmed in New York overnight.

The New South Wales state government said on Tuesday it had selected Lend Lease Corp and Macquarie Bank to build an underground rail link between Bondi Beach and Bondi Junction in eastern Sydney. Lend Lease rose 29.4 cents to A$28.294, while Macquarie bank dipped 12 cents to A$11.30.

News that Coca-Cola Amatil shareholders had approved a share-swap deal with San Miguel of the Philippines was already discounted and went by barely noticed. The stock fell 30 cents to A$16.90 after a 52 cent rise on Monday.
Casino operator Crown Ltd ended five cents higher at A$2.18 with almost 22 million shares traded.
Software systems group Computershare jumped 95 cents to A$9.45 in modest volume after it said it had placed 2.29 million shares with The Royal Bank of Scotland Plc.

In other markets, Australian bonds put in a solid performance as the market found favour with offshore investors and remained underpinned by expectations of an imminent rate cut after the Reserve Bank meeting.
A late surge took the September 10-year futures contract to its highest close since it became active in mid-June, with the yield on the benchmark bond ending back below 7.0 percent.
The Australian dollar recovered from Monday's 17-month lows, courtesy of aggressive buying of A$ against the Canadian dollar.
By 4.45 pm (0645 GMT) the local currency was perched at US$0.7525/30 having flown up from US$0.7453/58 late Monday.
